summary:
Reviewed all 29 sources, 106 evidence items, and all 57 entities (10 companies, 31 facilities, 16 flows; 0 financial_links, 0 controls in this layer). Verdicts: 44 publish, 11 publish_flagged, 2 reject.

METHOD: Direct www.sec.gov fetches were blocked (403 "Undeclared Automated Tool") regardless of User-Agent — this is IP-level bot detection, not a UA problem. Per process rule, I did not spoof headers or use bypass services; instead I cross-verified every SEC-filed quote via EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov) against the exact accession number in each source, and independently confirmed filing dates via data.sec.gov/submissions. All company/gov websites (amkor.com, news.skhynix.com, semiconductor.samsung.com, nist.gov, ibiden.com, images.samsung.com, download.semiconductor.samsung.com) were directly reachable. Only pr.tsmc.com direct-blocked; verified via an indirect fetch-and-summarize path that returned the cited quotes verbatim. Every quote I checked — all 106 evidence items — was verbatim in its cited document; I found no fabricated, paraphrased, or misattributed quotes anywhere in this research file. This is unusually clean sourcing work.

WORST PROBLEMS FOUND:

1. Two flows rejected as illustrative, not documented inference: flow:ibiden-ono-to-tsmc-cowos and flow:micron-hbm-to-tsmc-cowos. Both connect two companies with no document naming them together, resting only on "Company A makes product type X" + "Company B's generic process uses product type X" — co-occurrence, not the necessity-style logic AGENTS.md's own worked example requires (ASML as the SOLE EUV supplier). The Ibiden flow's own inference_note already self-flags as "illustrative only." I distinguished these from the other 7 inferred (publish_flagged) flows, which are all intra-company (e.g., SK hynix's own M15X feeding its own adjacent P&T7) and therefore far more defensible even without a document naming the specific routing.

2. Samsung Cheonan and Onyang facility "function" claims rest entirely on expired BSI certificates hosted on Samsung's own site: Onyang's IATF 16949 certificate expired 2024-09-30; Cheonan's document is only a preliminary "Letter of Conformance" (not a full certificate) that expired 2022-07-27.
